ambition: SOTA-level coding and engineering capability inside the declared compact parameter/compute class, without GPT-class parameter stacking.

shared_core.token_readout: autoregressive token decoder used only as the language interface
role: encode prompt, repository, code context, and explicit constraints
produce shared contextual token states without dominating model capacity
receive zero-gated residuals from hierarchy, typed attention, CFM, and generated experts

structured_output.scope: all structured AST, patch, tool-action, diagnostic, and engineering JSON outputs

typed_channels.role: indentation, delimiters, grammar, AST-like block structure
identifiers, declarations, imports, API references, call relations
task intent, document plan, segment roles, patch rationale
tests, compiler diagnostics, runtime errors, numerical checks
Triton kernels, Linux systems, profiling, latency, memory and I/O constraints

semantic_channel_attention.source: floorplan semantic channel and slot attention

borrow: explicit allowed relation mask per channel
typed_cross_attention.memory: global + syntax + symbol + discourse + execution + engineering tokens

mita_sparse_routing.source: MiTA route attention used by floorplan/chip lines
mita_sparse_routing.use: route long repository and document context without dense all-token attention

slot_mixing.use: exchange plan, API, test, and systems constraints before token decoding

input: training-only tests and diagnostics during training
stage_a_ast.target: canonical language-specific AST graph with node types, lexical values, parent-child edges, and scope/symbol relations

hierarchy.level: leaf grammar, lexical values, and symbol anchors

stage_b_result.condition: Stage-A generated AST only during primary inference
training_curriculum: early: teacher AST for stable content-flow learning
middle: target AST mixed with generated and perturbed AST
stage_b_result.target: code, patch, and engineering result conditioned on the generated AST

cfm.inference: Stage A generates AST first; Stage B consumes only that generated AST and emits the result through the standard token decoder. Target AST is never available at inference.
cfm.ablation_rule: The two-stage claim requires a matched one-stage control that conditions directly on prompt/repository state without target AST.

training_scopes.purpose: separately train syntax, symbol, discourse, execution, and engineering representations
isolate the benefit of cross-channel routing
learn plan/segment/span flow without perturbing the base model

train: all hierarchy, fusion, and language heads

training_scopes.purpose: learn E synthesis and reallocate capacity inside the fixed tier

execution_order: train typed cross-attention and MiTA fusion only
optional generated-expert stage after matched controls pass

experimental_arms.name: one-stage result CFM control
components: direct result CFM conditioned on prompt/repository state

promotion_gates: No component is promoted by parameter count alone.
Typed channels are individually trainable and independently measurable.
Cross-attention-only training must beat the frozen base before joint training.
Two-stage AST-first CFM must improve AST validity and executable success, not only latent MSE.
Stage B primary evaluation must consume only Stage-A generated AST.
All structured outputs must achieve 100% strict JSON validity through native model structure.
Final model stays at or below the 23M primary claim cap.
Final inference is static and reports total resident parameters and FLOPs.
The SOTA claim is restricted to the frozen low-capability benchmark class.
evidence_boundary: This is an architecture contract. No coding or engineering quality result exists yet.
